questions.coherence: One design. M18.210 adds convertCollectionLibrary beside the SVG path and reuses rightsOf, witnessSessions and the existing iconifyShapePack and importedShapePack builders; it does not add a third pack builder. M18.211 puts the version rule behind one predicate (packHasFonts/isFontFormat) and replaces every scattered '1.1' compare, which closes cp30 F5's concern for good. M18.212 reuses core's categoryTitle as the single fallback rule for both the encoder and the panel, and the studio feeds names through the existing catalog merge (listed() dedups by id, catalog names win). The harness pair is consistent: M18.223 calls last-ci and ci-run-red rather than re-deriving CI state, and M18.222's reporter reaches only the root Vitest run, because testStepEnv strips FLUXION_TEST_DURATIONS. One inconsistency: M18.222's standard (rule 23, 'at most half on every OS') and its implementation (a CI warning, nothing tracked) disagree at HEAD (F1).

findings.summary: M18.222 measures timeout headroom, but its first readings list four bounded-time tests over 50% of their timeout on ubuntu, three of them NFR-SEC-001 cases; nothing tracks them, and rule 23 says no test may be over half.
findings.evidence: The CI warning step lists them. Ubuntu verify at 9565074 (job 125397514379): font-subset-save '1.6 MB recorded range' 15566/20000 ms (78%), cli.pack-import refusals 65072/90000 (72%), cli.pack-import 50-SVG corpus 73714/120000 (61%), drawio '16 Mi library work budget' 11781/20000 (59%), import-svg 50-SVG corpus 10100/20000 (51%). At c699c7a (job 125413287653): refusals 73%, drawio budget 72%, corpus 65%, font-subset 64%. macOS and Windows list 0 in both runs. cp32's disposition required each listed security case, 'and any others found', to assert a step or ratio bound or be shown under 50% on all three OSes. The landed row names only two cases, and the commit was closed before its own CI reading existed. testing.md rule 23 (same commit) states 'A unit test uses at most half its timeout on every OS', which is false at HEAD. The CI step ends in '|| true' and only warns. Neither progress.md nor the backlog mentions the listed tests.
findings.failure_scenario: The drawio budget case, which rose from 59% to 72% between two consecutive runs, or the font-subset range case passes 100% on a loaded ubuntu runner under coverage. Main goes red again, the stream's work stops, and another 'Main green again' row speeds up code. That is the cp32 F1 loop, now with a warning nobody reads.
findings.fix: A row that takes the listed tests from the last three completed ci runs (test-headroom --run x3). Each NFR-SEC-001 case asserts its bound as a step count or scaling ratio, with the timeout an outer guard: drawio 16 Mi budget, font-subset 1.6 MB range (already a ratio, so cut its absolute work or fixture size), and cli.pack-import refusals (split into per-refusal cases, each with its own bound). The corpus cases are shown under 50% or given a measured reason. No timeout is raised. After that, the CI headroom step fails (no '|| true') when a test exceeds 50% on two consecutive runs of the same OS, or the gates leg reads it. Record the readings in progress.md.

findings.summary: The red-landing refusal accepts any historical red run as Fixes-ci, does not name the red run or job, and has no case for a pending run with a failed job, though cp32's disposition asked for all three.
findings.evidence: ciRefusal passes when ci-run-red.mjs <id> --since <upstream> exits 0. That script (scripts/gates/ci-run-red.mjs:33-37) accepts any ci or gates run with a failed job whose head is an ancestor of upstream. 'Fixes-ci: 41426181149' (6d45a30, chromium 2/4, a runner fault) would let any product commit land while an unrelated red holds main. The refusal text is "main's ci is red (last-ci exit N)", with no run id or job. land.test.mjs covers a completed failed run only, not the M18.191 pending-with-failed-job path that produced cp32 F2. The commit's own review recorded the first gap as R11 F2 and left it open. The 'feat(' match also misses scope-less 'feat:' subjects (R11 F1).
findings.failure_scenario: During a long red, a stream cites the red run it fixed earlier, or any red run, on an unrelated feature commit, and land.mjs lets it through. Main then stacks a second change on an unexplained red, as a6a2ef5 and 5028ff7 did.
findings.fix: Pass last-ci's red run id(s) (the newest completed red, or the pending run with a failed job) into ciRefusal, and accept Fixes-ci only when it names one of those. Name the run and failed job(s) in the refusal. Add harness cases for a pending run with a failed job, a stale red run cited as Fixes-ci (refused), and 'feat:' without scope.
